To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a collision tumor of small lymphocytic (SLL) lymphoma and oropharyngeally located squamous cell carcinoma can be mistaken for an ‘unknown primary’ and the diagnosis can be missed if not considered in the differential diagnosis.
the incidental finding of tonsillar lymphoma obscured a primary HNSCC in a patient with cervical lymph node SCC.

a rare occurrence of a tonsillar collision between a microscopic human papilloma virus-positive squamous cell carcinoma and small lymphocytic (chronic lymphocytic) lymphoma was incidentally detected during a workup for a metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the neck.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a rare collision of two tumors, HNSCC and SLL in the tonsil, and the importance of pathologists’ awareness of such an occurrence in the workup of cervical lymph node metastasis of unknown primary.
the presentation of a rare occurrence of a microscopic tonsillar SCC metastasis obscured by SLL, a collision tumor, in a patient with a known cervical SCC metastasis.
the rare occurrence of tonsil involvement by SLL and its potential to mask a microscopic SCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this case represents an unknown occurrence with a known primary.
the patient had SLL obscuring microscopic tonsillar SCC.
this was a collision tumor of SLL and HNSCC, with the latter obscuring the former.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a thorough search for the occult primary is warranted even if lymphoma is detected in the neck and tonsillar region.
a small occult SCC of Waldeyer’s tonsillar ring may be obscured by lymphoma and may be mistaken for an unknown primary tumor.
the diagnosis of an unknown primary HNSCC with a synchronous SLL of the tonsil is a rare event.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful search and sampling of the Waldeyer’s lymphoid ring is necessary in all cases of cervical lymph node SCC with unknown primary.
the workup for occult HNSCC should include an assessment for lymphoma and other malignancies.
the workup for an occult HNSCC must be thorough and meticulous to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment.
